title: From vision to reality: AMLA Chair Bruna Szego speaks at 29th Euro Finance Week

paras.text: Returning to Euro Finance Week one year on, Szego reflected on how the Authority is turning its vision of one coherent EU response to money laundering and terrorist financing into concrete action. With risks evolving rapidly amid geopolitical change and technological advances, she underlined that an effective response depends on connecting information and expertise across institutions and borders.

She highlighted the progress made in 2026. AMLA will have delivered 15 of its 40 regulatory mandates by the end of the year, prioritising those with the greatest practical relevance for industry, such as customer due diligence. Together with national authorities, it is developing a common supervisory methodology, while calibrating its selection model for the direct supervision of up to 40 financial institutions and groups from 2028. On financial intelligence, AMLA has consulted on common formats for suspicious transaction reports and put in place the framework for joint analyses, with the first ready to launch.

Looking ahead, Szego described 2027 as a decisive year of implementation and selection, as the AML Regulation begins to apply and AMLA continues to grow from around 190 staff today to more than double that by the end of next year. She encouraged institutions to make the necessary adjustments in good time and thanked them for their engagement so far.

She concluded that the shared commitment of AMLA, national supervisors, FIUs, law enforcement and the private sector offers a unique opportunity to build a more effective and integrated AML/CFT framework for the EU.
